title: Five brothers, one ship

facts.text: On 13 November 1942, the light cruiser USS Juneau was torpedoed by the Japanese submarine I-26 off Guadalcanal and sank in less than 20 seconds.
Juneau had already been damaged in a savage night battle off Guadalcanal a few hours earlier.
Aboard were five brothers from Waterloo, Iowa: George, 27; Frank, 26; Joe, 24; Matt, 23; and Al, 20.
They had enlisted in the Navy together on 3 January 1942, on the condition that they serve together.
More than 100 men survived the sinking, but the rescue did not come for days, and only ten were ever picked up. The last was found nine days later.
All five Sullivans died. Frank, Joe, and Matt were killed in the explosion; Al died of his wounds; George was lost from a raft days afterward.
Their parents, Thomas and Alleta, learned on 12 January 1943, when three uniformed men came to the door. Thomas asked, 'Which one?' The officer answered, 'I'm sorry. All five.'
Thomas and Alleta then toured the country for war bonds, asking that none of their sons die in vain.
Alleta Sullivan christened a new destroyer named USS The Sullivans on 4 April 1943. Their sister, Genevieve, joined the WAVES.
Their loss led the War Department to adopt what became known as the Sole Survivor Policy.

sources.title: The Sullivan Brothers: The Loss of USS Juneau (CL-52), Naval History and Heritage Command

declassified.fact: The wreck of Juneau was found on 17 March 2018, St. Patrick's Day, by the research ship Petrel, lying about 13,000 feet down off the Solomon Islands.

13 November 1942. The light cruiser USS Juneau, already damaged in a savage night battle off Guadalcanal, was torpedoed by the Japanese submarine I-26 and sank in less than 20 seconds.

Aboard were five brothers from Waterloo, Iowa: George, Frank, Joe, Matt, and Al, aged 20 to 27. They had enlisted together on the condition that they serve together. All five died.

Their parents learned on 12 January 1943, when three uniformed men came to the door. Their loss led the War Department to adopt what became known as the Sole Survivor Policy.
